title: 行李费涨价：航司竟省下7.5%税，谁在买单？
speaker: Katy Nastro

segments.en: The price of airfare can rise. Cheap flights can also exist, but that doesn't necessarily mean that that is working for airlines.
segments.zh: 机票价格可能上涨，廉价航班也可能存在，但这并不一定意味着对航司有利。

segments.en: Airlines are really feeling the pressure from this additional cost, and they're looking at ways to protect their margins. So they're really looking to be creative here.
segments.zh: 航司正感受到额外成本的压力，他们正在想办法保护利润空间，所以会寻求一些创新做法。

segments.en: And one of such ways is looking at ancillaries like bag fees. And it's sort of a win-win for the airlines in this stage because, yes, they're getting extra revenue from these increased bag fees.
segments.zh: 其中一种方式就是行李费这类附加服务。现阶段对航司来说算是双赢，因为他们确实从提高的行李费中获得了额外收入。

segments.en: But then they're also not subject to a 7.5 excise tax that they put on base fares that they are subject to. So that's more money in the pocket, as well as they have now this framing, this justification of higher jet fuel prices.
segments.zh: 而且行李费还不用缴纳基础票价需缴纳的7.5%消费税，这样他们能留下更多收入，同时还能以油价上涨为由头。

segments.en: And they can always push back and say, you know what, you don't have to check a bag even though the prices have risen. But do travelers, can they just decide not to check a bag?
segments.zh: 他们总是可以反驳说，即使价格上涨，你也可以选择不托运行李。但旅客们真的能决定不托运吗？

segments.en: We asked that question for families that, unfortunately, are feeling the pressure of having or needing to check a bag. So it's really a win-win for the airlines, and they lose, lose for travelers, especially when, yes, base fares have increased domestic prices for summer.
segments.zh: 我们向那些不得不托运行李的家庭提出了这个问题。所以这对航司来说是双赢，对旅客来说则是双重损失，尤其是夏季国内基础票价已经上涨。

segments.en: Just for example, according to our Going data, up 18% international fares, up 7.5%. So unfortunately, this summer specifically is really going to be challenging for that cost-conscious traveler.
segments.zh: 根据我们的Going数据，国际票价上涨18%，国内上涨7.5%。所以不幸的是，今年夏天对注重成本的旅客来说将尤其具有挑战性。
